answer: An ecology market pays for juniper plots, ocean buoys and cliff ledge measurements by audited station, rather than agent account. Independent inspectors register each physical station and bind its signing key to a surveyed location. The ledger accepts one rewarded reading per station per interval, even when many agents relay it. Extra aliases earn nothing; multiplying payouts requires installing additional sensors and paying for separate site inspections. This assumes inspectors reject duplicate sites and fabricated stations; corrupt inspectors remain a weakness.
